plain_english_policy: Enactment of HB365 would expand eligibility for the State Employees' Health Insurance Plan (SEHIP) in Alabama to include specific retired or former state employees. Specifically, it allows judges of probate and legislators who retire with benefits from their respective funds to continue coverage by paying full costs. Additionally, any person serving in the legislative, judicial, or executive branches who has worked for 24 consecutive months and is at least 50 years old can elect to keep health insurance after leaving employment if they pay all associated costs (including premiums) as prescribed by the group insurer. The bill limits coverage under this new provision to the former employee and their dependents only, not extending it to other family members beyond that scope.
policy_direction_if_enacted: The policy direction is to provide a pathway for certain state employees—specifically those in long-term service (24+ months) who are over age 50—to maintain health insurance coverage after leaving state employment, provided they assume full financial responsibility. This creates an optional continuation of benefits that shifts the cost entirely from taxpayers to the individual former employee.
sponsorship_supports_position: Representatives Fields, Vance and Grimes affirmatively advanced this bill.
evidence_quotes: "any person serving in the legislative, judicial, or executive branches of Alabama having served for 24 consecutive months and having attained the age of 50 years may elect to continue participation in the State Employees' Health Insurance Plan when the person leaves employment if the following conditions are met"
"The entire cost for the insurance shall be paid by the former employee under such terms and conditions as the group insurer may, from time to time, prescribe."
"Coverage shall be limited to the former employee and dependents of the former employee."
